lead: The first update separates two ChatGPT usage changes and reports a proposed sale of sensitive chatbot data under legal challenge. Directly confirmed photography guidance, child-safety reporting and hardware tracing keep their scopes explicit; bare-metal inference and desktop wrappers remain demonstrations with different dependencies.

The late-morning update pairs concrete human review of generated expressions with competing accounts of AI privacy and security. Market rotation, memory shortages and reported shipment restrictions remain dated observations rather than universal conclusions; vendor offers and personal complaints keep their evidence limits visible.

The afternoon adds primary-grounded Google access-policy reporting, evaluation results with clear setting limits, and tools for historical retrieval and approximate model-state transfer. Rumored releases and broad mathematical claims remain separated from verified identity, independent proof checking and account-level availability.

sections.title: A confirmed photo-assignment restriction has a precise version scope
sections.intro: The Verge reports direct Times confirmation, without establishing that every image from Photoshop is generated.

sections.title: Two ChatGPT usage changes should not be collapsed into one
sections.intro: A model-specific correction and a limited shared-meter rollout describe different mechanisms and leave individual entitlements unchecked.

sections.title: Bankruptcy data objections concern a proposed transaction
sections.intro: Attorneys general challenge a chat-data auction, distinct from the separate intellectual-property license.

sections.title: Child-safety investigation and chip tracing retain evidence boundaries
sections.intro: Talkie's reported store removal is not a universal shutdown; corporate ownership and allegations are not guilt.

sections.title: A minimal operating system and a desktop wrapper make different tradeoffs
sections.intro: Bare-metal inference is a limited project demonstration; Claude artifacts retain host-app, permission and sharing dependencies.

sections.title: Software craft and mathematical excitement remain interpretation
sections.intro: An episode description and a selected quotation add perspective, not a verified product release or theorem.

sections.title: Human review works best when the question is concrete
sections.intro: A restricted-language study asks users to judge distinguishing scenarios, not simply approve an opaque expression.

sections.title: Private AI claims and data-access allegations require different evidence
sections.intro: An interview advocates privacy-preserving services; a separate Reuters excerpt reports a researcher's access allegation without the full incident details.

sections.title: Security automation reporting is not a compromise detector
sections.intro: Microsoft-attributed threat intelligence describes behavioral patterns and familiar techniques, without establishing every incident claim.

sections.title: Market rotation and supply constraints operate at different levels
sections.intro: Software performance, memory procurement pressure and a reported shipment pause retain their own dates, sources and limits.

sections.title: A membership offer, a music game and a complaint are not comparable benchmarks
sections.intro: Vendor pricing, interface descriptions and social allegations require different kinds of validation.

sections.title: A second index adds no independent cryptographic verification
sections.intro: The newer feed framing points to Aaronson's existing post; secret algorithm claims remain unverified.

sections.title: Google access rules have dates and defined data categories
sections.intro: Primary Google documents ground the policy report; they do not authorize any account migration.

sections.title: Rumored releases and cost tuning remain different kinds of inference
sections.intro: Selected outputs, token statistics and launch billing corrections do not establish secret model identity or company motive.

sections.title: Effort and boundary behavior depend on the evaluation setting
sections.intro: Goodhart and Siren separate task effects, misaligned behavior and safeguards without converting test rates into production probabilities.

sections.title: A mathematical weekend and selected optimizer results are not universal verification
sections.intro: Authors describe useful progress, web-assisted cases and limits that broad superhuman headlines can obscure.

sections.title: Cached history and translated state reduce different costs
sections.intro: Time Machine controls retrieved dates; speculative encoding approximates model state with measurable retention limits.

sections.title: Model lineage and context workflows need cautious interpretation
sections.intro: Timing fingerprints are indirect, while setup advice and a swarm audit remain individual workflows.

sections.title: Video scale adds creative control and a post-training tradeoff
sections.intro: MAGI-2 reports stronger output while noting that some pretrained reasoning became harder to elicit.

sections.title: Privacy pilots and router claims do not replace a threat-model audit
sections.intro: A limited OpenAI test and a startup profile describe different services and levels of evidence.

sections.title: Power and consciousness essays depend on their assumptions
sections.intro: Subjective concentration forecasts and proposed non-conscious architectures are arguments, not present empirical verdicts.

sections.title: Style and authority are cultural questions, not authorship tests
sections.intro: Essays and selected quotations question institutional authority and homogenized expression without establishing AI provenance.

sections.title: Financing, components and a researcher move carry distinct scopes
sections.intro: VC allocation reports, Avicena's raise and Shihipar's move do not establish a shared product outcome.
